summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update21.json → valid=true). Final direction this turn was a liveness question on the membership-change admission path, resolved as a source-explained negative. The helper that opens the configuration-change channel returns nil unless the latest configuration is committed and the leader has committed an entry in its term, and it carries a note that a transition of those conditions from outside the leader loop would need the loop to be kicked. Reading the writers answers it: for a running leader the latest configuration index is written inside the loop by the configuration-append path (raft.go:1235-1240) and the commit index plus committed configuration index are written inside the loop by the commit-notification handler (raft.go:786-800), while replication goroutines only advance the commitment object's internal match indexes and notify the loop. The loop re-evaluates the select after each such handler, so an accepted change request cannot be left waiting on a condition that has already become true; the only receive-side writer of the latest configuration index — a same-term appendEntries carrying a configuration entry — either drives the node out of the leader state in the same handler or applies to a transfer candidacy, which is not in the leader loop. Recorded as one Fact plus an 'explained' interpretation, with the maintenance caveat kept explicit: the note is a constraint on future writers of those fields, and adding one outside the loop would reintroduce the missed-wakeup hazard. Counterevidence preserved (the leader-term start index is fixed for the term, and the same-term-appendEntries case is not a counterexample because it coincides with leaving leadership). In this turn I also read the NetworkTransport request/response path (sendRPC, decodeResponse, the InstallSnapshot streaming call) and found no defect: receiver error text is propagated to the caller and connections are released on decode failures, with the streaming RPC deliberately closing its connection.
